title: Long-term Intravital Immunofluorescence Imaging of Tissue Matrix Components with Epifluorescence and Two-photon Microscopy
protocol: Culture B16-F10-GFP melanoma cells in a 10 cm Petri dish using DMEM + 10% FBS media.
When the cells are 80-90% confluent, wash them with PBS and detach them by trypsinization.
Spin down cells at 1,500 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml Ringer's solution and transfer it into a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Spin again and remove all supernatant except a thin layer of medium that stays just above the pellet.
Resuspend the cells to end up with a thick cell slurry.
Anesthetize the mouse with a mixture of ketamine/dorbene [medetomidine] (75mg/kg-1mg/kg).
Confirm that the animal is sufficiently anesthetized by performing a gentle toe pinch.
Increase the isoflurane concentration in steps of 0.1 % in case movements are observed (e.g., withdrawal of the paw).
Keep mouse on a rectal thermistor controlled heating pad at 37 °C during the whole procedure.
Protect its eyes with an appropriate ophthalmic ointment.
Prepare a Hamilton syringe (33 G needle, 10 ml syringe volume).
Remove the tip cap with the needle and load 20 µl of cell slurry on top of the tip chamber.
Pull back the plunger until 5 ml slurry is loaded inside the syringe.
Remove the excess slurry from the tip chamber and close the tip cap.
Fix the proximal edge of the ear on the tip of an index finger using adhesive tape.
In a 45° angle, slowly insert the Hamilton syringe needle between dorsal dermis and the cartilage.
Once inside, penetrate the ear proximal to distal for about 2-3 mm.
Place the needle horizontally to the ear skin and insert it slowly into the ear dermis.
Press the plunger once the needle end is in the skin to initiate cells inoculation in the skin.
Shave the mouse head and depilate the hairs around the head.
Anesthetize the mouse with a mixture of humidified oxygen and isoflurane.
Confirm that the animal is sufficiently anesthetized by performing a gentle toe pinch.
Increase the isoflurane concentration in steps of 0.1% if movements are observed.
Keep the mouse on a rectal thermistor controlled heating pad at 37 °C throughout the procedure.
Protect the eyes with appropriate ophthalmic ointment.
Build a platform made out of glued glass histology slides.
Turn the mouse onto its back.
Gently place the tumor-bearing ear on the stack of glass slides.
Fixate the anterior and posterior edges of the ear to the stack using small stripes of adhesive tape.
Cut the ventral skin of the mouse pinna along the antihelix using a scalpel.
Gently peel off the ventral dermis and cartilage from the dorsal dermis where the tumor was inoculated with curved tweezers.
Pull off the ventral skin and cartilage with curved forceps, exposing the dorsal dermis.
Keep the opened ear skin wet by using Ringer's buffer and protect the humidity by using a coverslip.
If persistent bleeding occurs from tumor vessels, stop the bleeding by adding 100 µl thrombin (5 U/ml) in Ringer's buffer on top of the ear for 5 min.
Wash the ear twice with approximately 5 ml of Ringer's buffer and remove extra liquid with sterile wipes.
Immediately proceed to the next step without allowing the open ear to dry.
Fold the part of the ear with the open dermis into the eminentia conchae.
Dry the outer unopened ear dermis with sterile wipes.
Apply 0.5 μl of surgical glue to the anterior and posterior dorsal edges of the ear.
Flatten the dorsal ear dermis onto the glass slide.
Apply primary antibodies targeting extracellular matrix molecules at a concentration of 10 µg/ml in a total volume of 100 µl blocking buffer to the exposed ear.
Cover the ear with a cover slip.
Incubate for 15 min.
Wash the ear twice with approximately 5 ml of Ringer's buffer.
Apply secondary antibodies or streptavidin conjugates at a concentration of 10 µg/ml in a total volume of 100 µl blocking buffer to the exposed ear.
Cover the ear with a cover slip.
Incubate for 15 min.
Wash the ear twice with approximately 5 ml of Ringer's buffer.
Euthanize the animal 7 days after inoculation of GFP-B16-F10 melanoma on the back skin of congenic mouse.
Collect spleens from euthanized animals.
Isolate splenocytes with mechanical disruption of the spleen through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Label splenocytes for 8 min at 37 °C with Red CMTPX cell cytoplasm stain (1 μM in PBS).
Wash labeled splenocytes 4 times in 15 ml at 4 °C.
Inject labeled splenocytes with 200 μl serum-free medium into the tail vein of mouse whose ears were inoculated with B16-F10-GFP 7 days earlier.

Add freshly prepared sterile ascorbate-Ringer's buffer containing 140 mM sodium ascorbate, 10 mM HEPES, 4 mM KCl and 5 mM CaCl2 at a pH of 7.5 (ascorbate-Ringer's buffer final osmolarity 320 mOsM) on top of the immobilized ear for short-term imaging.
Cover the ear with a coverslip and start imaging by using a fluorescence stereomicroscope with 2X lens for short-term imaging.
Place the outlet of a needle (connected to a reservoir containing ascorbate-Ringer's buffer) under the coverslip, about 0.5 cm away from the ear for long-term imaging.
Use a peristaltic pump at a speed of 1 µl/min to constantly deliver ascorbate-Ringer's buffer to the chamber under the coverslip for long-term imaging.
Change the 1X lens to a 2X lens.
Open and configure the acquisition software settings for the fluorescent stereomicroscope.
Choose 12 bit as the image color depth in camera settings.
Adjust the grey-scale range from 0% to 5.1%.
Set gamma correction to 2.
Set acquisition gain to 1 (minimum).
Set fluorescence intensity to 1,000 (maximum).
Set magnification between 280X and 320X.
Adjust exposure time to less than 1 second.
Configure the time interval for acquisition cycle between 1 to 2 minutes depending on the number of imaging fields.
Choose several fields containing tumor cells and stained ECM proteins.
Acquire images from appropriate fluorescent channels using a motorized stage over time (e.g., every 2 min).
Euthanize the anesthetized mouse by cervical dislocation followed by exsanguination.
Build a circular wall of about 2 cm diameter and 2-3 mm height around the ear using silicon grease.
Ensure there are no leaking points in the silicon grease barrier.
Fill the circle with ascorbate-Ringer's buffer.
Place the mouse on the stage and connect the heating pad (set to 37 °C).
Open the acquisition software and configure the settings of the multiphoton microscope.
Choose up to four different fields that contain tumor cells and stained ECM proteins.
Tune the Ti-Saphire laser to 850 nm for GFP signal and subsequently use a single photon 647 nm for fluorophore 647 staining.
Visualize fibrillar collagens with second harmonic generation (SHG).
Acquire images of the appropriate fluorescent channels, such as GFP and fluorophore 647.
Acquire SHG images over time, e.g., every 2 minutes.
Use a water immersion HCX APO 20X lens with 1.00 NA and 2 mm working distance for imaging.
Euthanize the anesthetized mouse with cervical dislocation followed by exsanguination (intracardiac perfusion).
